questions.question: By the California ISO's own reported total interchange, what share of its demand was met by net imports in August 2026, in percent?
questions.answer: Using EIA's own reported total interchange, net imports met 8.29 percent of CAISO's demand in August 2026 (ba_supply_monthly, variable net_import_total_interchange_share_pct, entity eia930:CISO). The row covers all 31 days of the month, and it is not flagged as a thin month. The ERW derives this table from EIA-930 data. The figure comes from EIA's total interchange. The other measure in the table is the demand-less-net-generation balance, which reads 19.66 percent for August. The warehouse notes that CAISO's balance reads about 10 points higher than its flows from December 2025, because EIA's published net generation for CAISO dropped then.

This is the mean of 168 hourly day-ahead prices (spp_dam) for each hub, Monday 19 to Sunday 25 October 2026 in Central time (iso_dam_hub_prices). West averaged 27.25 USD/MWh and North averaged 25.73 USD/MWh. The difference, West minus North, is 1.52 USD/MWh. The window was whole, with 168 of 168 hours held.
